chapter_note: Heavy dialogue-frame chapter. The first half (i=0-42) is dominated by the disciple's elaborate autobiographical question about why he is sometimes at peace, sometimes disturbed — this functions as dialogue setup, not cosmological substrate, even though it uses substrate vocabulary (Mind, Wisdom, other body, Arche). The substrate teaching proper begins at i=46 with the Apostle's answer, which lays out a clear cosmological-physiological mapping: soul wearing body → Mind of Light coming with Wisdom and Hearing → disturbance through stars/powers above + bitter members coming in via food/water → Sin in body. This is genuine substrate teaching about the cosmic mechanics of psychic disturbance. A recapitulation passage (i=70 and i=93-103) uses the "I have made known unto thee" hortatory voice but restates substrate content. Closing dialogue at i=104-109 returns to frame. Heavy lacunae throughout (70.9% damage).
